modelAnswer:
Paragraph 1: A few weeks later, when I almost forgot the contest, there came the news. My essay about Paul Revere’s horse had won first prize! At first I thought there must be a mistake. How could someone who found writing so painful beat everyone else? But my teacher showed me the letter, and there was my name. At the award presentation, I walked onto the stage with shaking legs. As the prize was handed to me, I looked for my teacher in the crowd. He was clapping louder than anyone else.

Paragraph 2: I went to my teacher’s office after the award presentation. I wanted to thank him, but the words got stuck in my throat. He smiled and said, “I told you that you had a good shot.” I admitted that I had almost refused to try, and that without his push I would never have known I could write. He laughed and said the horse was not the only one who had kept going. Then he handed me a notice about another writing contest. This time I did not say no. I took it, thanked him again, and walked out already wondering what story I would tell next.

questions.question: 人物
questions.answer: 续写里动笔的是两个人：原本怕写作、被老师劝去参赛的“我”，和欣赏“我”讲故事、又逼“我”一遍遍重写的社会学老师。

questions.question: 视角与风格
questions.answer: 第一人称“我”回忆中学往事，一般过去时；短句很多，带一点自嘲的幽默；人物的话很少，只有老师两处短的直接引语，其余都靠叙述。续写也用第一人称过去时，多用短句，直接引语只留一两句。
evidence: I got tired. I had doubts. I wanted to quit.

questions.question: 待解决问题
questions.answer: 原文停在“我”终于写完文章、享受写作、不再在乎输赢；还没交代的是比赛结果，以及“我”对一直推着自己的老师怎样回应。
evidence: If I didn’t win, I wouldn’t care.

characters.name: 我
characters.role: 来自巴西家庭、英语是第二语言的中学生，故事的讲述者

lines.label: 性格
lines.text: 怕写作，但答应了就肯下苦功，一遍遍查拼写、请姐姐改语法。
lines.evidence: I worked hard. I checked my spelling.

lines.label: 此刻
lines.text: 从一心想赢变成享受写作本身，输赢已经不重要。
lines.evidence: the thought of winning had given way to the enjoyment of writing

characters.name: my social studies teacher
characters.role: “我”的社会学老师，劝“我”参赛的人

lines.label: 想要
lines.text: 看中“我”会讲故事，想让“我”发挥这个长处。

lines.label: 表现
lines.text: 爱笑，看“我”表演时笑得最响，读到文章也会大笑。
lines.evidence: No one laughed harder than he did.

lines.label: 性格
lines.text: 鼓励之外也严格，夸完就让“我”重写。

sourceLinks.sourceQuote: No one laughed harder than he did.
sourceLinks.use: 第 1 段颁奖时，让老师在台下鼓掌最响，呼应他当年看“我”表演时笑得最响。

sourceLinks.sourceQuote: I think you have a good shot at this.
sourceLinks.use: 第 2 段在办公室里，老师用 good shot 提醒“我”他当初就相信“我”能行。
第 2 段结尾老师递来下一次比赛的通知，“我”这次没有拒绝，和开头的不假思索地拒绝形成对照。

taskCard.route: 第 1 段写获奖消息和颁奖时的反应，第 2 段在老师办公室道谢，用“我”接过下一次比赛的通知收住“我”对写作的转变。

paragraphs.must: 说清传来的是比赛的消息；第二段首句说“颁奖之后”，所以第一段要写到颁奖仪式，并让“我”在场。“我”得奖是原文最支持的路线，得几等奖是本文的选择。
paragraphs.draft: “我”得知写保罗·里维尔的马的文章得了一等奖，不敢相信；看到通知上的名字才信了。颁奖时“我”腿发抖上台，看到老师在人群里鼓掌最响。
paragraphs.bridge: 颁奖一结束，“我”特意去找老师，是要对他说什么？

paragraphs.must: 以“我”到老师办公室开头，写清两人见面说了什么、做了什么，并收住原文留下的问题：这次经历让“我”怎样看待写作。
paragraphs.draft: “我”想道谢却说不出口；老师提起当初那句 good shot，“我”承认差点不敢试。老师笑着说坚持下来的不只是那匹马，又递给“我”下一次写作比赛的通知，“我”这次没有拒绝。

standard.essay:
Paragraph 1: A few weeks later, when I almost forgot the contest, there came the news. My essay about Paul Revere’s horse had won first prize! At first I thought there must be a mistake. How could someone who found writing so painful beat everyone else? But my teacher showed me the letter, and there was my name. At the award presentation, I walked onto the stage with shaking legs. As the prize was handed to me, I looked for my teacher in the crowd. He was clapping louder than anyone else.

Paragraph 2: I went to my teacher’s office after the award presentation. I wanted to thank him, but the words got stuck in my throat. He smiled and said, “I told you that you had a good shot.” I admitted that I had almost refused to try, and that without his push I would never have known I could write. He laughed and said the horse was not the only one who had kept going. Then he handed me a notice about another writing contest. This time I did not say no. I took it, thanked him again, and walked out already wondering what story I would tell next.

notes.role: 交代消息是什么，写“我”从不信到确认，再把场景推到颁奖台上，为第二段的“颁奖之后”铺好路。

items.quote: At first I thought there must be a mistake.
items.explain: 一个怕写作的人得了奖，第一反应是不信，这比直接写“我高兴极了”更符合原文里“我”的样子。

items.quote: How could someone who found writing so painful beat everyone else?
items.explain: 借原文 difficult and painful 的意思，用一个问句写出“我”的怀疑，也让读者想起“我”原来多怕写作。

items.quote: He was clapping louder than anyone else.
items.explain: 呼应原文 No one laughed harder than he did：老师还是那个最捧场的人。用动作写老师的骄傲，不用写“他很为我自豪”。

notes.role: 在办公室里写“我”向老师道谢，把原文的伏笔一一收回，最后落在一个具体动作上。

items.quote: the words got stuck in my throat
items.explain: 想说却说不出来，用一个看得见的反应写激动和感激，不堆眼泪和拥抱。

items.quote: “I told you that you had a good shot.”
items.explain: 全文唯一一句直接引语，借原文老师的 good shot，让他用自己的话轻轻点出“我早说过”。

items.quote: the horse was not the only one who had kept going
items.explain: 回收原文 like Revere’s horse, I kept going，老师用玩笑把“我”和那匹马连在一起，幽默也合原文语气。

items.quote: This time I did not say no.
items.explain: 和开头 I said no without thinking 对照，短短一句就写出“我”的变化，不需要再讲道理。

expressions.expression: the words got stuck in my throat
expressions.function: 写感激或激动到说不出话，比 I was very moved 具体，适合第二段见老师的场面。

expressions.expression: walked onto the stage with shaking legs
expressions.function: 用身体反应写紧张，让怕写作的“我”上台领奖的场面可信。

expressions.expression: walked out already wondering what story I would tell next
expressions.function: 用一个正在进行的念头收尾，写出“我”已经开始期待下一次写作，不用喊口号。

pitfalls.pitfall: 第一段就写“我”跑去找老师、写两人的对话
pitfalls.why: 第二段首句才写“我”颁奖后去老师办公室，第一段提前写见面，第二段就没东西可写，还会前后重复。

pitfalls.pitfall: 结尾写“我”从此爱上写作、成了作家，或加一句“坚持就是胜利”
pitfalls.why: 原文已经说 the enjoyment of writing，再升华只是重复；结尾应落在一件具体的事上，比如接过新的比赛通知。

pitfalls.pitfall: 让父母、姐姐或新同学来推动情节，比如由别人告诉“我”去感谢老师
pitfalls.why: 续写的主角是“我”和老师；姐姐在原文只帮忙改语法，让旁人推动转折会分走两个主要人物的戏。

advanced.essay:
Paragraph 1: A few weeks later, when I almost forgot the contest, there came the news. My teacher stopped me in the hallway, waving a letter, and announced that Paul Revere’s horse had galloped all the way to first place. I stared at him, sure he was joking. Me, the kid who had once acted out the Titanic because a written paper felt impossible? But my name was printed right there on the letter. On the day of the award presentation, my knees shook as I climbed onto the stage, and my hands were so wet that I nearly dropped the certificate. When I looked down at the audience, I spotted my teacher in the front row. Just as he had laughed harder than anyone at my play, he now clapped harder than anyone else.

Paragraph 2: I went to my teacher’s office after the award presentation. He was marking papers, but he put down his pen the moment I knocked. I had practised a thank-you speech all the way there, yet all that came out was, “I really didn’t think I could do it.” He leaned back and grinned. He reminded me that I had once turned him down without a second thought, and said that a horse who kept going through the night deserved a writer who did the same. Then he pulled a sheet of paper from his drawer. It was a notice for next year’s contest. “Well?” he asked. This time I didn’t need to be persuaded. I folded the notice into my pocket, thanked him again, and hurried home to hunt for a new subject, one that, like Revere’s horse, nobody else would think of.

beyondStandard.quote: Paul Revere’s horse had galloped all the way to first place
beyondStandard.explain: 用 galloped 把获奖说成那匹马一路跑到第一，延续原文拿马开玩笑的口吻，比 had won first prize 更有味道。

beyondStandard.quote: Me, the kid who had once acted out the Titanic because a written paper felt impossible?
beyondStandard.explain: 用原文“演泰坦尼克号”的旧事写怀疑，细节更具体，也更像原文叙述者的自嘲。

beyondStandard.quote: a horse who kept going through the night deserved a writer who did the same
beyondStandard.explain: 老师的话改成转述，又把马和“我”并列，比标准版的玩笑更完整，也合原文少用直接引语的写法。
